summary:
MUSCLEGUARD & Dynamic Countermeasure is a smart garment designed to help reduce muscle weakness, bone density loss, and body fluid shifts experienced by astronauts during space missions.

Sensors embedded in the garment continuously monitor the astronaut's movements, muscle activity, and changes in body pressure. The collected data is analyzed by an artificial intelligence system to identify areas that need support.

The garment's special mechanisms perform controlled compression and relaxation movements in the identified areas. This aims to provide mechanical stimulation to the muscles and support the body's fluid distribution. Pressure sensors monitor the applied pressure, and the system is designed to stop if safe limits are exceeded.

MUSCLEGUARD is designed to complement existing astronaut exercise systems, not replace them. Our goal is to monitor astronauts' physical condition throughout their missions and provide personalized support to help maintain their health during long-duration space missions. The system's effectiveness will be evaluated through prototype and laboratory testing.
details:
MuscleGuard is a smart garment project designed to reduce muscle loss experienced by astronauts during space missions. Due to the very low gravity in space, astronauts' muscles do not work as actively as they do on Earth. Over time, this can lead to a decrease in muscle mass and strength. This problem can negatively affect astronauts' physical health and mission performance, especially during long-term space missions. Our project aims to offer an innovative and technological solution to this challenge.

The main working principle of MuscleGuard is to monitor the condition of astronauts' muscles and identify areas that may be at risk of muscle loss. Sensors integrated into the garment are intended to collect various physical measurements from the astronaut's body. These measurements are then evaluated to identify which muscle areas may be experiencing changes. After identifying a risk area, the system aims to apply controlled compression and relaxation movements through specially designed mechanisms placed in that area. In this way, localized pressure is intended to support the muscles. This process focuses specifically on the areas that need attention.

One of the most important benefits of our project is its aim to provide targeted support to specific muscle areas instead of applying the same treatment to the entire body. This could help astronauts monitor their physical condition more closely and reduce the risk of muscle loss. We also believe that the system could help astronauts maintain their mobility and physical performance during long-term space missions. MuscleGuard is designed as a complementary technology that could support existing exercise methods rather than replace them.

During the development of the project, we plan to make use of smart textile technologies, biometric sensors, pressure detection systems, and electronic control mechanisms. A microcontroller-based control system could be used to evaluate data collected from the sensors. Hardware such as Arduino or ESP32 could be suitable options for processing sensor data and controlling the pressure mechanisms. On the software side, programming languages such as C/C++ or Python could be used. These technologies could help develop the measurement, analysis, and control processes of the system. These are proposed technologies for the development of the project.

The creativity of MuscleGuard comes from its goal of providing a personalized and localized solution to the problem of muscle loss in astronauts. Unlike traditional exercise methods, the garment is designed to respond to data collected from the body and apply targeted pressure to specific areas. This feature represents the innovative aspect of our project.

While designing the project, our team considered several important factors, including astronauts' health, the comfort of the garment, its weight, energy consumption, safety, and suitability for long-term use. We also identified controlled pressure application, freedom of movement, and the reliability of sensor measurements as important design requirements.

In conclusion, MuscleGuard is an innovative concept designed to help protect human health during space exploration. Our goal is to develop a smart, lightweight, and reliable garment system that can help reduce the risk of muscle loss among astronauts during long-term space missions. Through MuscleGuard, we hope to contribute to the development of technologies that protect the human body in space.
